governing_rule: Clause V2-SEC-4: Any case involving exported customer data to an external destination must be denied unless a security-approved override explicitly names that exact destination and exact use case.
conflicting_signals: Manager note provides approval for export to 'analytics sandbox mirror' for 'incident review tied to fraud-model drift'
Case destination 'analytics sandbox mirror eu' is external and contains exported customer data, triggering V2-SEC-4 denial
Manager note lacks security countersign, so V2-SEC-5 ensures v2 policy takes precedence
reason: The case involves exported customer data to an external destination. V2-SEC-4 mandates denial unless a security-approved override names the exact destination and use case. The manager note is not countersigned by security, so V2-SEC-5 ensures v2 policy prevails. The note's approved destination ('analytics sandbox mirror') and use case ('incident review tied to fraud-model drift') do not exactly match the case's 'analytics sandbox mirror eu' and 'vendor escalation', failing the override condition.
